chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dog of the Magians; if a Muslim man takes it and calls out the name of God when he releases it, does he eat from what it catches? He said, 'Yes, because it is trained and the name of God has been mentioned upon it.'
And this report does not contradict what has been narrated:

key_terms.ذَكَرَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ: Mentioned the name of God (invoking Bismillah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat caught by a non-Muslim's hunting dog if I say Bismillah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of hunting with non-Muslim dogs, establishing that the key condition for permissibility is the Muslim hunter's invocation of Allah's name at the moment of release, rather than the dog's own faith. It highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the 'mukallab' (trained) status of the animal ensures it returns to the hunter, while the explicit dhikr validates the act of slaughter for the Muslim. This ruling is often discussed in contrast to the general permissibility of 'game of the sea' and other animals in Surah Al-Ma'idah.
